thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: A managed robotic-workforce service supplying robot arms, site integration, teleoperation fallback, maintenance and replacement for high-mix manual tasks at a flat monthly fee. The company states that customers need the outcome addressed by its described product; precise quantified pain was not independently verified. Verified current scope: workstation/cell; company-reported deployments only. Stated ambition: multi-line/fleet/site. Public evidence supports responsibility for hardware, models/policies, integration, commissioning/qualification, remote operations, ongoing support/maintenance and hardware financing/RaaS; supports only partial/shared responsibility for robot body, end effectors/tooling and simulation/training. Overall integration responsibility is classified as full_prime. Commercial evidence: 2_first_party_deployment_claim; technical evidence: 3_vendor_documented. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Direct integration comparator: public evidence supports company responsibility for both delivered integration and commissioning/customer acceptance.
